correctness.rationale: Exact spectral projector decomposition of B=J-I gives four orbit probabilities. Their off-index sum equals (2-2cos(nt))/n² <=4/n² at every real time, so a uniform expected matrix would force n<=4. For n=3 an exact four-atom law gives all four probabilities 1/6 in expectation; for n=4 direct substitution at pi/4 gives all four 1/8. Exact fraction verifier evaluates the four-time table and independent finite matrix exponentials corroborate the formulas. Hypotheses and probability-law quantifiers are explicit.

value.rationale: A naturally motivated complete graph-family classification answers when arbitrary observation-time randomization can restore uniform quantum mixing in crown graphs, identifies an unexpected positive C6 case previously known to fail instantaneous/Cesaro uniformity, and proves an unrestricted sharp negative result for every n>=5. It exposes a structural mismatch between classical average and selectable sampling distributions.
